blocking.issue: The error-code area for a fail-closed State Store failure contradicts 01-system-overview. System overview says a `failureMode: closed` Policy such as `ai.token-budget` rejects with `RZ-STS-<NNN>` when the State Store slows down. This document says a closed failure in a request Phase uses 'an RZ-<AREA>-NNN code of the type's area', which gives RZ-AI for `ai.token-budget` and RZ-RL for `ratelimit` or `quota`. STS is a foundation error-code area, and the two documents assign the same event to different areas.
blocking.evidence: 02 L369: "| A request Phase, `onRequestHeaders` through `onUpstreamRequest` | Rejects with 401 or 403 for auth and authz types, otherwise 503, and an `RZ-<AREA>-NNN` code of the type's area |"; 02 L365: "a State Store call fails or exceeds `stateStoreTimeout`"; 01 L253: "A `failureMode: closed` Policy, such as the `ai.token-budget` default, rejects with `RZ-STS-<NNN>`"; foundation-pack L51: "areas: `CFG`, `RT`, `UP`, `AUTH`, `RL`, `PLG`, `AI`, `CP`, `STS`"
blocking.fix: Change the L369 `closed` cell to: "Rejects with 401 or 403 for auth and authz types, otherwise 503; the code is `RZ-STS-NNN` when a State Store call failed or timed out, `RZ-PLG-NNN` when a Plugin trapped or exceeded limits, and otherwise an `RZ-<AREA>-NNN` code of the type's area (`AUTH`, `RL`, `AI`)". Also check L416 ("an `RZ-RL` or `RZ-AI` code owned by the feature document"): it covers a missing Consumer quota, not a State Store failure, so it can stay, but say so explicitly.

ac_results.ac: Kind catalog gives a schema sketch with required fields for every kind: Gateway, Route, Upstream, Policy, Plugin, Consumer, AIProvider, AIModel, Environment and Cluster.
ac_results.note: Ten H3 sketches mark required fields with '# required'. Environment explicitly states every spec field is optional and that promotion.from is required when promotion is set. Every list carries its x-ruralz-list type.

ac_results.ac: Attachment and precedence includes a worked example that resolves Gateway-, Route- and Upstream-scoped Policies (Route over Gateway; Upstream-scoped Policies apply to the upstream leg only).
ac_results.note: The worked example table covers slot replacement (cors), inheritance (jwt-default), stacking (ratelimit), per-leg Upstream Policies (upstream-oauth on orders only) and a replaced Policy.

ac_results.ac: Complete annotated example Bundle covers REST aggregation, a gRPC Route, an AI Route with AIProvider and AIModel, a WASM Plugin and a Consumer.
ac_results.note: orders-summary (aggregate), cart-grpc, support-chat with anthropic-prod/openai-prod and AIModel support-chat, Plugin geo-block with Policy geo-block-default, Consumer partner-acme.

ac_results.ac: CEL expressions and allowed places contains a table of every place CEL is allowed, with the variables available in each.
ac_results.note: Allowed places table has 16 rows with Variables and runtime-error columns, plus a Variables table. Every x-ruralz-cel field used in the sketches appears in it.

ac_results.ac: The document states that JSON is accepted as a strict subset of YAML and states the KrakenD import stance (ruralz bundle import krakend, best-effort fidelity levels, Planned (M2)).
ac_results.note: L33 covers JSON as a strict subset. L63 covers `ruralz bundle import krakend`, Planned (M2), best-effort, fidelity levels exact/equivalent/approximate/manual.

ac_results.ac: Validation and diff semantics specifies the diff output format in both JSON and human-readable form.
ac_results.note: Human-readable and ruralz.diff.v1 JSON examples agree: counts 5/1/1/3, a move with a one-based and a zero-based position, and exit codes.

ac_results.ac: Secrets are referenced only via secretRef, and env substitution supports ${VAR} and ${VAR:-default}.
ac_results.note: secretRef section, RZ-CFG-012 for inline literals, Environment substitution section with ${VAR} and ${VAR:-default}.
